entries.title: Google Groups settings explained
entries.summary: Every Google Groups for Business setting (Admin console wizard, org-level sharing settings, and the full groups.google.com settings page) with defaults and precise behaviour: who can post vs moderation vs spam, replies and Reply-To, post as group, Collaborative Inbox, per-member delivery, DMARC rewriting, limits and deletion. Helios creates groups and members; these settings are changed in Google.
entries.content:
**Last verified: September 2026.** Google renames settings and moves help pages often (Admin Help now lives at knowledge.workspace.google.com; the old support.google.com/a links redirect). Where this article says "check", check Google's current page before relying on it. Anything marked *unverified* comes from community or third-party sources, not Google.

## What Helios does and doesn't do here

Helios creates Google groups (address, name, description) under [[nav:/admin/groups|Admin > Groups]], adds and removes members with a role, deletes groups, and keeps the group list in sync. Its offboarding "release address" step can also create a group on a departed person's old address (see the recipes article). Helios does **not** change any of the settings described below: everything on groups.google.com (who can post, moderation, Collaborative Inbox, replies, delivery) and the Admin console access grid is set in Google's own UI. A group Helios creates gets Google's defaults for your organization, which is why a freshly created group often "doesn't work" until you finish it in Google. Per-member delivery settings are also not exposed in Helios today.

**Group scenarios (preview).** When an admin turns on *Group scenarios*, Helios can also create a group from a scenario based on the recipes article: it applies the recipe's settings through the Groups Settings API, sets per-member delivery for the members it adds, reads everything back and reports any value Google did not keep. This needs the optional `apps.groups.settings` delegation scope and the Groups Settings API enabled in the Cloud project; without them, plain group creation works as before. Settings the API cannot set (the standard footer, subject prefix, auto replies, shared labels, who can attach files, allow email posting) stay manual and are listed with each scenario.

## Where the settings live

There are three places, and they overlap:

| Place | What you set there | Who |
|---|---|---|
| **Admin console** > Directory > Groups > *Create group* wizard, and later the group's *Access settings* page | Group information (name, address, description, owners), the access-type presets (Public, Team, Announcement only, Restricted, Custom), the access grid, who can join, external members, aliases, and "Group settings" (a subset of the groups.google.com page) | Super admins and Groups admins |
| **Admin console** > Apps > Google Workspace > Groups for Business > *Sharing settings* | Organization-wide policy that constrains what group owners may do (external members, external email, who can create groups, default visibility) | Admins |
| **groups.google.com** > the group > *Group settings* | Every group-level setting, including many the Admin console does not show (moderation, spam handling, replies, subject prefix, footer, Collaborative Inbox) | Group owners and managers, and admins |

Admin console settings and groups.google.com settings are the same underlying Groups Settings API values; whichever you saved last wins. The Admin console wizard shows the most important ones with friendlier wording.

Sources: [Create a group in your organization](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/groups/create-a-group-in-your-organization), [Group settings reference](https://support.google.com/groups/answer/2464926), [Set organization-wide policies for using groups](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/groups/set-organization-wide-policies-for-using-groups).

## Organization-wide settings that override group owners

Admin console > Apps > Google Workspace > Groups for Business > Sharing settings. Google's page states the defaults below.

| Setting | Options | Default | What it really does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Accessing groups from outside this organization | Private / Public on the Internet | Private | Whether any group's web archive can be visible to people outside the organization at all. Private means "Anyone on the web" is never offered at group level. |
| Creating groups | Only admins / Anyone in the organization / Anyone on the Internet | Anyone in the organization | Who may create groups from groups.google.com. Admin-created groups are unaffected. |
| Group owners can allow external members | on/off | **off** | When off, the group-level "Allow external members" switch is greyed out for owners. Google notes this does **not** stop an **admin** allowing external members for a specific group in the Admin console or via the API. |
| Group owners can allow incoming email from outside the organization | on/off | **off** | Same pattern: when off, owners cannot let "Anyone on the web" post. Admins still can, per group. This is the number-one reason an external sender bounces. |
| Default for permission to view conversations | Owners / Owners and managers / All members / All organization users / Anyone on the Internet | All organization users | Only a default for **new** groups; owners can change it per group. |
| Group owners can hide groups from the directory | on/off | off | Enables the per-group "hide from directory" option (and a further "hide newly created groups" default). |

Edition notes: Groups for Business is included in Business Starter and up, Education and Nonprofits editions; Frontline and Essentials editions have restrictions (check the [Groups administrator FAQ](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/groups/groups-administrator-faq)). If the Groups for Business **service is turned off** for a user's organizational unit, groups still deliver email and still work for Drive/Calendar sharing, but that user gets no groups.google.com web UI: no conversation history, no moderation queue, no Collaborative Inbox.

## The Admin console "Create group" wizard

Step 1, *Group information*: name (max 73 characters), group email (max 63 characters before the @, some words are reserved), description, and the initial **owners**. Step 2, *Group settings*: an **access type** picker, the **access grid**, **who can join**, and **allow members outside your organization** (being renamed **Allow external members in the group**, with a new sub-option allowing only admins to add external users).

The access-type presets fill in the grid; picking anything in the grid afterwards flips the type to *Custom*. The grid has rows *Contact owners*, *View conversations*, *Post*, *View members*, *Manage members* and columns *Group owners*, *Group managers*, *Group members*, *Entire organization*, *External*. The commonly cited preset values are (*unverified*: Google does not publish the matrix, it is only visible in the wizard and documented by third parties):

| Preset | View conversations | Post | View members | Contact owners |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Public | Entire organization | Entire organization | Entire organization | Entire organization |
| Team | Entire organization | Entire organization | Members | Entire organization |
| Announcement only | Entire organization | Owners and managers | Entire organization (managers see the list) | Entire organization |
| Restricted | Members | Members | Members | Entire organization |

*Manage members* is always owners and managers unless you customise. In every preset the *External* column is empty; you tick it yourself, and only if the organization-wide setting (above) permits it or you are an admin.

**Q2 2026 change (important for external members).** Google now enforces a strict internal/external classification: a group with *Allow external members* **off** may contain only organization members, directly or through nested groups. Switching an external group to internal **permanently removes** its direct external members, and external members of a nested group are filtered out of an internal parent. Review the classification the Admin console assigned to existing groups before relying on them. Source: [Changes to internal and external classifications in Google Groups](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/groups/changes-to-internal-and-external-classifications-in-google-groups).

**Aliases.** Admin console > the group > *Aliases*: up to 30 alias addresses per group, on any verified domain; mail to an alias is treated exactly like mail to the primary address. Reserved words (abuse@, postmaster@ and a few others) may be blocked or behave specially. Source: [Give a group an additional alias address](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/groups/give-a-group-an-additional-alias-address).

## groups.google.com: every setting, tab by tab

Open groups.google.com, pick the group, click *Group settings* (gear). Labels below are Google's current ones; the API name in brackets is the Groups Settings API field, useful with GAM or scripts. Source for labels and options: [Group settings reference](https://support.google.com/groups/answer/2464926); API values: [Groups Settings API](https://developers.google.com/workspace/admin/groups-settings/v1/reference/groups).

### General

| Setting | Options | Default for a new work group | What it does / behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|
| Group name | text | (as created) | Shown in the directory and in the "via" rewriting (see DMARC below). |
| Group email | text | (as created) | Changing it re-addresses the group; the old address stops working unless you add it as an alias in the Admin console. |
| Group description | text | empty | Shown on the About page and in the directory. |
| Welcome message | text | empty | Emailed only to members who are **added directly**, not to people who join or are invited. |
| Enable additional Google Groups features | Off / Collaborative Inbox (`enableCollaborativeInbox`) | Off | Turns on Take/Assign/Complete and the status filters. **Requires Conversation history ON.** |
| Shared labels | on/off | off | Lets members apply group-wide labels to conversations in the web UI (labels do not travel into Gmail). |
| Who can see group | Group members / Organization members / Anyone on the web (`whoCanDiscoverGroup`) | Organization members | Whether the group appears in the groups.google.com directory. "Anyone on the web" needs the org-level Public setting. |
| Who can join group | Invited users only / Organization users only / Organization users can ask / Anyone can ask / Anyone can join (`whoCanJoin`) | Organization users can ask *(varies)* | Self-service joining. For a shared inbox or security@ choose *Invited users only*. |
| Allow external members | on/off (`allowExternalMembers`) | off | Greyed out for owners unless the org-level setting allows it. See the Q2 2026 note: turning it off removes external members. |
| Who can modify group details | Owners / Managers / Members | Owners and managers | Name, description, welcome message. |
| Who can view conversations | Owners / Managers / Members / Organization / Anyone on the web (`whoCanViewGroup`) | org default (All organization users) | Who can read the web archive. Does not affect email delivery to members. |
| Who can post | Owners / Managers / Members / Organization / Anyone on the web (`whoCanPostMessage`) | Organization members *(varies by preset)* | Who is **allowed** to send to the address. This is a permission, not a moderation rule: allowed senders are delivered (subject to spam handling and moderation, below); everyone else is rejected. |
| Who can view members | Owners / Managers / Members / Organization (`whoCanViewMembership`) | Organization members | Who can see the member list on the web. |

### Member moderation

| Setting | Options | Default | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|
| Who can manage members | Owners / Managers / Members (`whoCanModerateMembers`) | Owners and managers | Add, remove, change roles, approve join requests. Google's own troubleshooting says "can't manage members" is almost always this setting. |
| Who can modify custom roles | Owners / Managers | Owners | Edit the permission sets below. |
| Custom roles | create/edit | none | Named permission bundles beyond Owner/Manager/Member. Keep to the built-in three unless you need them; Helios shows only OWNER/MANAGER/MEMBER. |

### Member privacy

| Setting | Options | Default | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|
| Identification required for new members | Display name only / Either display name or organization profile / Organization profile and name | Either | What a joining member must show. Irrelevant for invite-only groups. |
| Who can contact group owners | Owners / Managers / Members / Organization / Anyone on the web (`whoCanContactOwner`) | Organization members | Controls the "Contact owners" form and the special `<group>+owners@` address. For a public group leave it at *Anyone on the web* so a locked-out sender has a path to a human. |
| Who can view member email addresses | Owners / Managers / Members | Managers | Hides addresses in the web member list. Email headers are unaffected. |

### Posting policies

| Setting | Options | Default | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|
| Allow email posting | on/off | on | Off means mail to the address is refused; the group becomes web-only. |
| Allow web posting | on/off (`allowWebPosting`) | on | Off hides "New conversation" on the web. |
| Conversation history | On / Off (`isArchived`) | On for Collaborative Inbox templates, otherwise **check** | OFF: messages are delivered to members but **not stored**; the web view stays empty; Digest/Abridged delivery and Collaborative Inbox cannot be used; the Groups Migration API cannot import. Turning it back on does not recover earlier mail. Source: [Turn conversation history on or off](https://support.google.com/a/users/answer/6103429). |
| Who can reply privately to authors | Owners / Managers / Members / Organization / Anyone | Members | Controls the web UI "Reply to author" button. It does **not** stop someone hitting Reply in Gmail, which goes to the author anyway. |
| Who can attach files | Owners / Managers / Members / Organization / Anyone | Members *(check)* | Governs attachments on **web** posts. Community reports (2025, *unverified*) say email posts with attachments from non-allowed senders are still delivered; do not rely on it as a security control. |
| Who can moderate content | Owners / Managers / Members (`whoCanModerateContent`) | Owners and managers | Approve, reject, delete messages; mark *Duplicate* / *No action needed* in a Collaborative Inbox; receive the spam report. |
| Who can moderate metadata | Owners / Managers / Members (`whoCanAssistContent`) | Owners and managers | *Take*, *Assign*, *Mark complete*, tags. For a helpdesk set this to **Members** or nobody can take a ticket. |
| Who can post as group | Owners / Managers / Members (`membersCanPostAsTheGroup`) | Owners and managers *(check)* | Who may choose the group address as the From when posting or replying **on the web**. Has no effect on Gmail's "Send mail as". |
| Default sender | Author's address / Group address (`defaultSender`: DEFAULT_SELF / GROUP) | Author's address | Which From is preselected on the web. *Group address* makes every web post look like it came from the group and **hides the original sender**; Google's troubleshooting page tells you to switch back to *Author's address* when "the original sender isn't shown". |
| Message moderation | No moderation / Moderate messages from non-members / Moderate all messages (`messageModerationLevel`) | No moderation | **Who**-based holding. Held messages go to *Pending* and wait for a content moderator. Independent of spam handling. |
| New member restrictions | No posting restriction / New member posts are moderated / New members cannot post | No posting restriction | Applies for a period after joining; useful for public discussion lists, pointless for invite-only inboxes. |
| Spam message handling | Reject all messages marked as spam / Moderate and notify content moderators / Moderate without notifying content moderators / Post suspicious messages to the group (`spamModerationLevel`: REJECT / MODERATE / SILENTLY_MODERATE / ALLOW) | **Moderate and notify content moderators** (API default MODERATE) | **Content**-based holding, applied even when Message moderation is *No moderation*. Suspicious mail lands in *Pending*. High-confidence spam is rejected regardless. |
| Rejected message notification | on/off + optional text (`sendMessageDenyNotification`, `defaultMessageDenyNotificationText`) | off | Sends a note to the author when a **moderator rejects** a pending message. It is not what bounces a non-allowed sender (that bounce is automatic). |

### Email options

| Setting | Options | Default | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|
| Subject prefix | text | empty | Prepended to every delivered subject, e.g. `[hello]`. Modifying the subject can invalidate the original sender's DKIM signature on the relayed copy (secondary source, *unverified*); Google's own ARC seal covers this for Gmail recipients. |
| Email footer | Include the standard Groups footer / Include a custom footer (max 1,000 chars) (`includeCustomFooter`, `customFooterText`) | standard footer on *(check)* | The standard footer adds an unsubscribe/"view on web" line; external recipients of a public contact inbox usually should not see it. |
| Group email language | language | organization language | Language of system mail (moderation notices, footers). |
| Auto replies | four toggles: members inside org / non-members inside org / members outside org / non-members outside org, each with text | off | Groups-level auto-responder, e.g. "Thanks, we reply within 2 business days". Sent per message, no rate limit documented; be careful with mailing-loop risk and keep it short. Work/school accounts only. |
| Post replies to | All group members / Group managers only / Group owners only / Message author only / Sender's choice / Custom address (`replyTo`: REPLY_TO_LIST / REPLY_TO_MANAGERS / REPLY_TO_OWNER / REPLY_TO_SENDER / REPLY_TO_IGNORE / REPLY_TO_CUSTOM) | Sender's choice (REPLY_TO_IGNORE) | Sets the `Reply-To` header on delivered copies. *All group members* forces replies back into the group and **drops the outside author** from a plain Reply. *Sender's choice* leaves the headers alone, so Reply goes to the author and Reply all goes to author + group. |
| Conversation mode | on/off (threading by subject) | on *(check)* | Off: every message with a matching subject starts a new conversation. |

## Email footers and disclaimers

*Include the standard Groups footer* appends, to every **member's** copy, the group's web link and an unsubscribe line ("To unsubscribe from this group... send an email to <group>+unsubscribe@..."). Outsiders writing in never see it, but a member's Gmail reply may quote it back to the customer. For a contact inbox (recipes a, b, c, e) it is noise: turn it off. A *custom footer* (up to 1,000 characters) is the place for a short signature line or a link to a privacy notice. Keep it short; a long legal disclaimer in a footer is mostly decoration, and if your counsel wants one they will tell you what it must say.

## Which settings matter in which recipe

| Setting | Matters most in |
|---|---|
| Who can post (+ org-level external email) | a, d, e, h: anything outsiders write to |
| Message moderation, Spam message handling | a, e, h: where a held message is a lost customer or a missed report |
| Post replies to | a, e (Sender's choice keeps the outsider in the reply); f (Author only stops reply-all storms); d (All members is fine) |
| Who can post as group, Default sender | a, b, c, e: replying as the group address |
| Enable additional Google Groups features, Who can moderate metadata, Shared labels | c (and a, b): Take, Assign, Mark complete |
| Conversation history | b, c, i (must be On); f, g, h (your choice) |
| Allow external members | d only |
| Per-member delivery | a (owner Abridged), e (everyone Each email), g (everyone No email) |
| Allow email posting | g (off) |
| Email footer, Subject prefix | a, e (off/empty), f (prefix useful) |
| Auto replies | a, e, h |

## How the pieces interact: the behaviours people trip over

**Permission vs moderation vs spam.** Three independent gates run in this order: (1) *Who can post* is a hard allow-list: a sender outside it is rejected with a bounce (Google does not document the exact text, but the NDR says the group does not allow posting from that address); the message never reaches Pending. (2) *Message moderation* holds allowed senders based on **who** they are (non-members, or everyone). (3) *Spam message handling* holds allowed senders based on **content**, regardless of (2). So "Who can post = Anyone on the web" with "No moderation" still holds some legitimate external mail in Pending whenever Google's classifier is unsure, and the default *Moderate and notify* only tells moderators in a **twice-weekly** report (Tuesday and Friday, Pacific time), not per message. Held messages are deleted after **14 days**; messages held as spam after **7 days**. Approving with *Approve author* whitelists that sender for future posts and supersedes moderation. Source: [Manage pending messages](https://support.google.com/groups/answer/2466386), [Legitimate email to a group marked as spam](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/support/troubleshooting/legitimate-email-to-a-group-marked-as-spam).

**High-confidence spam is always rejected**, whatever you choose; only "suspicious" mail is affected by the spam handling setting. The organization's Gmail spam and compliance rules apply on top, when the copy lands in each member's mailbox.

**A member does not receive their own post in their Gmail inbox.** Gmail suppresses the group copy of a message you sent yourself (it appears only in Sent). The message *is* in the group's web history if Conversation history is on. This is why the founder-style test "send to the group from my own account and see if it arrives" fails even when the group works. Test from a non-member or from a second member. Source: [Messages sent to an email alias or group aren't in my inbox](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/support/troubleshooting/messages-sent-to-email-alias-or-group-arent-in-my-inbox).

**Replying from Gmail.** The delivered copy carries the original `From:` (the outside sender) unless rewritten (see DMARC). In Gmail, **Reply** goes to that author only and **Reply all** goes to the author plus the group, provided *Post replies to* is *Sender's choice*. The outside person sees the member's own address as From, not the group, unless the member has Gmail "Send mail as" set up for the group address. Replies sent from Gmail with the group in To/Cc are posted to the group like any other message and appear in the history; replies sent only to the author never touch the group. Source: [Reply to a message](https://support.google.com/groups/answer/1046523).

**Replying from groups.google.com.** *Reply all* posts to the group and, with *Sender's choice*, includes the original external author; *Reply to author* is private. If *Who can post as group* includes you, a From selector lets you pick the group address; *Default sender* only chooses which is preselected. Replies posted as the group are delivered to the outside person with `From: <group address>` and are stored in the history. This is the path for a shared inbox where customers should only ever see hello@.

**Sending as the group from Gmail.** Gmail > Settings > Accounts and Import > *Send mail as* > add the group address. Google sends a **verification code to that address**, so you must be a member receiving mail from the group (or temporarily so) to complete it; keep *Treat as an alias* checked so replies to the group thread correctly. Mail is then sent by your account with the group address as From, DKIM-signed by your domain, SPF passes on Google's servers, and DMARC aligns. Nothing goes through the group, so the group history does **not** record it unless you also Cc the group. Sources: [Send emails from a different address or alias](https://support.google.com/mail/answer/22370), [Should I uncheck "Treat as an alias"](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/users/should-i-uncheck-treat-as-an-alias-in-gmail).

**DMARC and the "via" rewrite.** Groups relays each message to members with its own envelope sender (SPF passes for Google) and adds `List-ID`, `List-Post`, `Precedence: list` and `X-Google-Group-Id` headers. When the original sender's domain publishes DMARC `p=reject` or `p=quarantine`, Google rewrites the visible From to `Sender Name via Group Name <group address>` and moves the real address to Reply-To, so members' Reply still reaches the author. This cannot be turned off. Subject prefixes and footers modify the body/subject, which is why the rewrite exists. Gmail recipients also get an ARC seal that lets Google's own filters trust the relayed copy. Source: [DMARC and mailing lists / "via"](https://support.google.com/mail/answer/1311182).

**Group address as From when a member sends as the group**: SPF/DKIM/DMARC pass for your domain because Google signs it (see above). If you send as the group from an external mail system instead, that system must be authorised in your SPF/DKIM or DMARC fails.

**Attachments.** Message size limit is 25 MB (including attachments), the same as Gmail. Larger mail bounces from the group. *Who can attach files* is enforced on web posts; for email posts treat it as advisory (see the table).

**Conversation history OFF.** Delivery still works; Pending still works (moderators approve from the queue); nothing is retained afterwards, and web replies, digests, abridged delivery and Collaborative Inbox are unavailable. Turning it on later starts storing from that point only.

**Collaborative Inbox.** Adds *Take* (assign to me), *Assign* (with note; the assignee gets an automated email), *Mark complete*, *Mark no action needed*, *Mark duplicate*, plus filters *Assigned to me*, *Not assigned*, *Is unresolved*. Take/Assign/Complete need *Who can moderate metadata*; No action needed/Duplicate need *Who can moderate content*. Status lives only in the web UI: Gmail shows nothing, and reopening a resolved thread requires a new message or a manual status change. Shared labels are separate and also web-only. Forwarding from the web UI is limited to 25 recipients (*unverified*). Sources: [Use Collaborative Inbox features](https://support.google.com/a/users/answer/167430), [Set up a Collaborative Inbox](https://support.google.com/a/users/answer/10375787).

## Per-member delivery settings

Each membership has its own delivery option; it is **not** a group setting.

| Option (label) | API value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Each email | ALL_MAIL | Every message as it arrives. Default for members added through the Admin console or Helios. |
| Digest | DIGEST | Up to 25 full messages bundled into one email. |
| Abridged | DAILY | Up to 150 message **summaries** in one daily email. |
| No email | NONE | Read on the web only. Still counts as a member for permissions and Drive sharing. |
| (Disabled) | DISABLED | Set by Google when a member's address bounces repeatedly; fix the address and reset to Each email. |

Digest and Abridged need Conversation history ON. Where to set it: **the member** at groups.google.com > the group > *My membership settings* (or *My groups* > *Manage*). **An owner/manager or admin** can set it for someone else at groups.google.com > the group > *Members* > the member > *Subscription* column, or with the Directory API `members.patch` `delivery_settings` field (GAM: `gam update group <group> update member <user> delivery <allmail|digest|daily|none>`). The Groups Settings API does not carry it. The Admin console member list does not expose it today (*check*). Helios sets no delivery option, so members it adds get *Each email*. Sources: [Choose how often you get email from a group](https://support.google.com/groups/answer/9792489), [Directory API Members](https://developers.google.com/workspace/admin/directory/reference/rest/v1/members).

## Limits and deletion

From [Understand Groups policies and limits](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/groups/understand-groups-policies-and-limits): message size 25 MB; a group accepts at most **300 inbound messages per 5 minutes** from all senders combined and 1,800 per hour from any one sender; a group may send to 6,200,000 recipients per hour in total and 50,000 external recipients per day (5,000 per 10 minutes); membership per group is unlimited; a user can be a direct member of about 3,600 groups (about 9,000 including nesting) and own at most 1,500; up to 30 aliases; up to 200 members added per web session (10 external before a CAPTCHA). Hitting a limit restricts the group for about an hour, up to 24 hours. Note that the 300-per-5-minutes inbound cap is easy to hit with an automated sender (alerts, form notifications); use a user mailbox or a routing rule for those.

**Deleting a group** is immediate and permanent: the address starts bouncing, the conversation history is gone, Drive and Calendar items shared to the group lose that access, and there is **no restore window** (unlike users, which keep a 20-day window). Add the address as an alias somewhere first if mail must keep working. Source: [Delete a group](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/groups/delete-a-group-from-your-organization).

## Quick decision table

| You want | Set |
|---|---|
| Outsiders can email it, nothing silently held | Who can post = Anyone on the web; Message moderation = No moderation; Spam handling = Post suspicious messages to the group (or Reject); org-level external email allowed |
| Outsiders can email it, but reviewed first | Who can post = Anyone on the web; Message moderation = Moderate messages from non-members; someone checks Pending daily (14-day expiry) |
| Only staff can post | Who can post = Organization members (or Members) |
| Only the owners can post (announcements) | Who can post = Owners and managers; Post replies to = Message author only or Managers |
| Customers only ever see the group address | Who can post as group = Members; reply from groups.google.com choosing the group as From; or set up Gmail Send mail as |
| Members work tickets | Enable additional Google Groups features = Collaborative Inbox; Conversation history = On; Who can moderate metadata = Members |
| Nobody gets email, group is only for sharing | Every member = No email; Allow email posting off (optional) |

entries.title: Google Groups recipes: shared inboxes, security@, announcement lists and more
entries.summary: Tested-style configurations for common Google Groups uses: public contact inbox (hello@), shared mailbox replacement, Collaborative Inbox helpdesk, external client groups, security@/abuse@, announcement lists, Drive/Calendar access groups, a departed employee's address, and archive migration; each with wizard values, groups.google.com settings, per-member delivery, a test checklist, and the common mistakes that make a group 'not work'.
entries.content:
**Last verified: September 2026.** Every recipe below is written as a user story, then the exact configuration: Admin console wizard values, the groups.google.com settings that matter, per-member delivery, how to test it from a non-member account, what the sender and the members will see, and the common mistake with its symptom. Settings not listed keep Google's defaults; the companion article "Google Groups settings explained" covers every setting and why the defaults bite. Anything marked *unverified* is community practice, not Google documentation.

**Helios's part.** Create the group in [[nav:/admin/groups|Admin > Groups]] (address, name, description), add the members, then finish the settings below in Google. Helios does not set groups.google.com settings, the Admin console access grid, or per-member delivery; members Helios adds get *Each email*. Offboarding's "release address" step (recipe h) is the one place Helios creates a group on your behalf. With *Group scenarios* (preview) turned on, Helios can apply and verify these settings for recipes a to h; see the settings article.

**Before any recipe: the two org-level switches.** Admin console > Apps > Google Workspace > Groups for Business > Sharing settings. Both *Group owners can allow external members* and *Group owners can allow incoming email from outside the organization* default to **off**. Leave them off if you want admins to decide per group (an admin can still allow external per group in the Admin console); turn them on if group owners should be able to. Recipes a, d, e and h need external email allowed for that group one way or the other.

**Test accounts you need.** An external mailbox you control (a personal Gmail works; for the DMARC "via" check use a Yahoo or Outlook.com sender, since gmail.com publishes p=none), and a **second** organization account that is *not* a member. Your own posts to a group you belong to never show in your own Gmail inbox, so testing from your own account proves nothing.

## a) Public contact inbox (hello@ / info@)

*As a small business owner, I want customers to email hello@ and get a reply that comes from hello@, so that the business has one public address that outlives any employee, and I want one summary a day instead of every message.*

**Admin console wizard**: access type **Custom**. Grid: Contact owners = Entire organization + External; View conversations = Group members; Post = Group members **+ External**; View members = Group owners and managers; Manage members = Group owners and managers. Who can join = Only invited users. Allow members outside your organization = off. Owners: you.

**groups.google.com > Group settings**:

| Tab | Setting | Value |
|---|---|---|
| General | Enable additional Google Groups features | Collaborative Inbox |
| General | Who can post | Anyone on the web |
| General | Who can view conversations | Group members |
| General | Who can see group | Organization members (staff can find it) |
| Posting policies | Conversation history | On |
| Posting policies | Message moderation | No moderation |
| Posting policies | Spam message handling | Post suspicious messages to the group (occasional junk reaches the team) or Reject all messages marked as spam (occasional false positive is lost). Do **not** leave the default *Moderate and notify content moderators*: it holds real inquiries and reports them only twice a week |
| Posting policies | Who can post as group | Group members |
| Posting policies | Default sender | Author's address |
| Posting policies | Who can moderate metadata | Group members (anyone can Take a thread) |
| Email options | Post replies to | Sender's choice (**not** *All group members*, which drops the customer from a plain Reply) |
| Email options | Email footer | untick *Include the standard Groups footer* (customers must not see "unsubscribe") |
| Email options | Subject prefix | empty (a prefix is visible to the customer on replies) |
| Email options | Auto replies > non-members outside the organization | optional short acknowledgement |

**Per-member delivery**: the people who answer = **Each email**; the owner = **Abridged** (one daily summary; needs history on). Make the answering staff **Managers** so they can approve the rare held message and edit members.

**Working a thread**: open it at groups.google.com, click **Reply all**, change From to hello@, send; then **Take** and later **Mark complete**. Replying from Gmail works too but shows your personal address to the customer unless you set up Gmail *Send mail as* hello@ (the verification code arrives via the group, so do it while you receive Each email).

**What each side sees**: the customer's message lands in each Each-email member's inbox with the customer's name as From (or "Name via hello" when the customer's domain enforces DMARC), subject unchanged, no footer. A web reply as the group reaches the customer as `From: hello@` and sits in the thread. A Gmail Reply all reaches the customer from the staff member's own address and posts a copy to the group; a plain Gmail Reply reaches only the customer and the group never sees it.

**Test checklist**: (1) send from the external mailbox: all Each-email members receive it within a minute; (2) groups.google.com > Pending is empty; (3) reply all from the web as the group: the external mailbox receives it from hello@, the reply shows in the thread; (4) Reply all from Gmail: external mailbox shows the personal From, the group has the copy; (5) the owner's abridged summary arrives next day; (6) send from the Yahoo/Outlook.com address and confirm the "via" rewrite and that Reply still reaches it; (7) send from the non-member organization account and confirm delivery.

**Common mistake**: leaving spam handling on *Moderate and notify*. Symptom: a customer says they wrote a week ago, nobody saw it, and it is sitting in Pending (or was auto-deleted after 14 days).

## b) Shared mailbox replacement (a team working one address, history visible to members only)

*As an office manager, I want accounts@ to reach the three people in finance and let any of them see what the others have already answered, so that nothing is answered twice or missed when someone is away.*

**Wizard**: Custom; Post = Group members (+ External only if suppliers write to it); View conversations = Group members; View members = Group members; Manage members = Owners and managers; Who can join = Only invited users. **groups.google.com**: as recipe (a) with these differences: Who can post = Organization members or Anyone on the web as needed; Who can see group = Group members if it should not appear in the directory; Collaborative Inbox on so threads can be taken and closed; Post replies to = Sender's choice; footer off. **Delivery**: everyone Each email, or the lead on Abridged.

**What each side sees**: members get every message in Gmail; the "who answered what" view is only at groups.google.com (a Gmail reply appears there only if the group was in To/Cc). **Test**: from the non-member account send to accounts@; two members confirm receipt; one replies all from Gmail; the other sees the reply in Gmail and on the web; a plain Reply from Gmail does not appear on the web (expected).

**What you lose versus a real mailbox**: no shared Gmail folders or search across the archive from Gmail, no shared drafts, and no record of colleagues' plain replies. If the team needs those, a licensed user mailbox with delegation fits better (Helios offboarding sets delegation up; see the "User Offboarding" article).

**Common mistake**: Conversation history off. Symptom: mail delivers but the web view is empty and the digest option is greyed out.

## c) Queue / lightweight helpdesk with Collaborative Inbox

*As the person who runs IT for a 40-person charity, I want staff to email support@ and either of two volunteers to take a request, mark it done, and see what is still open, so that nothing falls through and we do not pay for a ticketing tool yet.*

**Configuration**: recipe (a) or (b) plus Who can moderate metadata = Group members; Who can moderate content = Owners and managers; General > Shared labels on, with labels like `access`, `hardware`, `billing`. Volunteers filter by *Not assigned* and *Is unresolved*, click **Take**, work the request, **Mark complete**. Assigning to someone else emails them.

**What each side sees**: the requester sees ordinary email replies; status, assignment and labels exist only at groups.google.com and never in Gmail. **Test**: from the non-member account send a request; volunteer A takes it (volunteer B sees "Assigned to A"); A replies all as the group; A marks complete; the *Is unresolved* filter no longer lists it; the requester replies again and the thread arrives as new mail but stays marked complete until someone changes it (expected).

**Limits before you call it a helpdesk**: no SLA timers, no reporting, no customer portal, no canned replies, no merge beyond *Mark duplicate*, resolved threads reopen only by hand, at most 300 inbound messages per 5 minutes, and no audit trail beyond the thread. It suits a few people and a few dozen requests a week. Beyond that, use an ITSM or helpdesk tool (commercial or open source); ObiLabs' Aegis is one option, but choose on fit.

**Common mistake**: Who can moderate metadata left at Owners and managers. Symptom: volunteers see no Take or Assign buttons.

## d) External client inquiry management (per-client or per-project groups with outside members)

*As a consultant, I want acme-project@ to reach my two colleagues and two people at Acme, so that the client can write to one address and never sees any other client's traffic.*

**Org level**: *Group owners can allow external members* on, or an admin allows it for this group. **Wizard**: Custom; Post = Group members + External; View conversations = Group members; View members = Group owners and managers (the client never sees a member list); Manage members = Group owners; Allow members outside your organization = **on**; Who can join = Only invited users. **groups.google.com**: Who can post = Anyone on the web (an Acme colleague who is not a member can still write in) or Group members (strict); Message moderation = No moderation; Spam handling = Post suspicious messages; Post replies to = All group members is acceptable here because every party *is* a member; Conversation history On; Who can see group = Group members; Who can view member email addresses = Managers; footer off. **Delivery**: Each email for everyone.

Privacy between clients comes from **one group per client**, never from roles inside one group. External members get email only; they cannot use the groups.google.com history unless org-level access is *Public on the Internet* and view-conversations allows it. Remember the Q2 2026 rule: if anyone later turns *Allow external members* off, the client members are removed permanently.

**What each side sees**: Acme people see messages from your staff's own addresses (or the group, if you reply as the group) and from each other; your staff see Acme's people as ordinary senders (possibly "via acme-project" if Acme enforces DMARC). **Test**: an Acme member sends and all four receive; the non-member organization account sends and is delivered (or bounced, per Who can post); a member of a *different* client group cannot open the history link.

**Common mistake**: adding the client with *Allow members outside your organization* off. Symptom: "Cannot add external member", or the client silently disappears from the member list after the Q2 2026 enforcement.

## e) security@ / abuse@ (reports delivered immediately, never moderated)

*As the person responsible for security, I want any outsider's vulnerability or abuse report to reach two trusted colleagues and me within a minute, so that a report is never held in a queue nobody checks.*

**Wizard**: Custom; Contact owners = Entire organization + External; Post = Group members + External; View conversations = Group members; View members = Group owners; Manage members = Group owners; Who can join = Only invited users; Allow members outside your organization = off.

**groups.google.com**:

| Tab | Setting | Value |
|---|---|---|
| General | Who can post | Anyone on the web |
| General | Who can view conversations | Group members |
| General | Who can see group | Group members |
| Posting policies | Message moderation | No moderation |
| Posting policies | New member restrictions | No posting restriction |
| Posting policies | Spam message handling | **Post suspicious messages to the group** (a false negative costs a minute of a human's time; a false positive costs a missed report) |
| Posting policies | Who can attach files | Anyone on the web (reports carry proof-of-concept files; advisory only) |
| Posting policies | Conversation history | On (you want the record) |
| Posting policies | Who can post as group | Group members (replies come from security@) |
| Posting policies | Default sender | Author's address |
| Email options | Post replies to | Sender's choice |
| Email options | Email footer | off |
| Email options | Auto replies > non-members outside the organization | optional receipt ("We received your report and will respond within N days") |

**Delivery**: every member **Each email**; no digests, ever. Add security@ to your `security.txt`. abuse@ and postmaster@ are reserved in places; create them as **aliases** of this group in the Admin console and test each alias separately.

**What each side sees**: the reporter's mail arrives as ordinary email from the reporter (or "Name via security"); the reporter sees the optional receipt immediately and your reply from security@ when you reply as the group from the web. **Test**: from the external mailbox send a report with an attachment; all members receive within a minute; Pending is empty; from the Yahoo/Outlook.com address send again and confirm the "via" copy still delivers; a member replies from the web as the group and the reporter sees security@; send to each alias.

**Common mistake**: creating the group in Helios or the Admin console and stopping there. Symptom: reports from outside bounce ("does not allow posting"), because a new group's Who can post does not include External and the org-level external-email switch is off.

## f) Internal distribution list / announcement-only list

*As the head of a school, I want all-staff@ to reach every employee, only the office to be able to send to it, and a reply to come back to me rather than to 60 people, so that announcements do not turn into a reply-all storm.*

**Wizard**: type **Announcement only** (Post = Group owners and managers; View conversations = Entire organization; View members = Group owners and managers; Manage members = Group owners and managers; Contact owners = Entire organization). Make the office staff Managers. **groups.google.com**: Who can post = Owners and managers; Post replies to = **Message author only** (a reply goes back privately to whoever sent the announcement) or *Group managers only*; Conversation history On (staff can read past announcements) or Off (pure blast, nothing kept); Subject prefix `[All staff]`; Collaborative Inbox off; standard footer off unless you want the "view on web" link. **Delivery**: Each email for all. If the list really is everyone, use a Helios dynamic group so joiners and leavers are automatic.

**What each side sees**: staff receive `[All staff] ...` from the manager who sent it; Reply goes to that manager; Reply all to the group address bounces with "does not allow posting" because members cannot post. Tell people that bounce is expected. **Test**: from a manager account send; a non-manager member receives; that member hits Reply all and gets the bounce; the manager receives the private Reply.

**Common mistake**: Post replies to = All group members on an announcement list. Symptom: a member replies and 60 people get a bounce or, if members may post, a reply-all storm.

## g) Department/team group for Drive files and calendar invites (access-control group, no email)

*As a team lead, I want a marketing@ group so that I can share a Drive folder and calendar invites to one name and stop editing sharing lists every time someone joins or leaves.*

**Wizard**: type **Restricted** (members only everywhere). **groups.google.com**: Allow email posting = off (keeps the address from becoming an accidental mailing list), Who can see group = Organization members (so people can pick it when sharing), Who can join = Only invited users. **Delivery**: every member **No email** (with posting off nothing arrives anyway). Share Drive folders and shared drives to the group address; put the group on calendar invites (Google expands it at invite time; later members do not get past invites). Membership changes take a few minutes to reach Drive. A Helios dynamic group fits here well.

**What each side sees**: nothing by email; members see the shared folder in *Shared with me* once membership syncs. **Test**: share a folder to the group from the non-member account; a member can open it; remove a member and confirm access disappears within a few minutes.

**Common mistake**: posting left on and members on Each email. Symptom: someone "emails the team" through the sharing group and the whole department gets a mailing list they did not ask for.

## h) Role address for a departed employee (catch mail after offboarding)

*As the manager of someone who left, I want mail sent to their old address to reach their replacement for a few months and tell outsiders whom to contact, so that customers do not get a bounce and the company keeps the account unlicensed.*

Google keeps a deleted user's address for about 20 days, and an existing user's address cannot be taken by a group while it exists. Helios offboarding's **release address** step handles the sequence: rename the account to `deprovisioned.<name>@`, remove the leftover alias Google leaves behind, then create the group `Former: <name>` on the old address with the chosen colleague as a member (see the "User Offboarding" article). Then finish in Google: Who can post = Anyone on the web (customers and vendors still get through); Message moderation = No moderation; Spam handling = Post suspicious messages or Reject; Conversation history On or Off as your retention policy dictates; Who can see group = Group members; Auto replies > non-members outside the organization = "This person has left; please contact X"; Post replies to = Sender's choice; footer off. **Delivery**: the replacement on Each email.

Alternatives: add the old address as an **alias** of the successor's mailbox (simpler, nothing kept separately) or a Gmail routing rule. Group-on-the-old-address is common practice rather than a Google-documented pattern (*unverified* as an official recommendation). Set a date to delete it; deletion frees the address immediately.

**What each side sees**: outsiders get the auto reply and their mail reaches the replacement, who sees the original sender as From. **Test**: from the external mailbox write to the old address; the replacement receives it; the external mailbox gets the auto reply; a plain Reply from the replacement reaches the outsider from the replacement's own address.

**Common mistake**: creating the group before the old alias is gone. Symptom: "entity already exists" on group creation; Helios's release step retries for this, but if you do it by hand, wait a couple of minutes after removing the alias.

## i) Groups as a destination for a migrated shared mailbox archive

*As an admin moving from Microsoft 365, I want the old shared mailbox's history to be readable somewhere after the move, so that the team can look things up without keeping a licensed mailbox.*

Documented but narrow: the [Groups Migration API](https://developers.google.com/workspace/admin/groups-migration) inserts RFC 822 messages **into the group's archive only**; nothing is delivered to members, and it requires Conversation history ON. Limits: 25 MB per message, about 10 requests per second, one message per call. Helios's Microsoft 365 migration planner can map a shared mailbox to a group for **new** mail; importing the old archive needs the API or a tool that wraps it (for example GAM, *unverified* syntax) and the `apps.groups.migration` scope, which Helios does not request. **What each side sees**: members find the imported mail only at groups.google.com, in the original order; Gmail shows nothing. **Test**: import one message and open it on the web; confirm no member received an email.

**Common mistake**: expecting imported mail to appear in Gmail. Symptom: "the migration ran but nobody got anything" (working as designed).

## Common mistakes and their symptoms (all recipes)

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Outside senders get a "does not allow posting" bounce | Who can post excludes External; or the org-level external-email switch is off and an owner (not an admin) tried to allow it | Set Who can post = Anyone on the web as an admin, or turn on the org switch and retry |
| Outside mail arrives days late, or never, with no bounce | Held in Pending by *Moderate messages from non-members* or by spam handling *Moderate and notify* (report only Tuesday and Friday; auto-deleted after 14 days, spam after 7) | Set No moderation and Post suspicious/Reject; check groups.google.com > Pending now |
| "I sent to the group from my own account and got nothing" | Gmail hides your own group copy | Test from a non-member or a second account; check the web history |
| Customer dropped from the reply | Post replies to = All group members forced Reply-To to the group | Set Sender's choice; train staff to Reply all |
| Customer sees a staff member's personal address | Reply from Gmail without Send mail as | Reply from groups.google.com as the group, or set up Send mail as |
| Everyone sees "via Group" instead of the sender | Sender's domain publishes DMARC reject/quarantine | Expected; cannot be disabled |
| Original sender hidden entirely on web posts | Default sender = Group address | Set Author's address |
| Nobody can Take or Assign | Collaborative Inbox off, or Who can moderate metadata excludes members | Enable additional features = Collaborative Inbox; set metadata to Members |
| Web view empty although mail delivers | Conversation history Off | Turn On (past mail is not recovered) |
| Digest option greyed out | Conversation history Off | Turn On |
| Owner can't add members | Who can manage members excludes their role | Set Owners and managers |
| Group not visible in the directory | Who can see group = Members, or hidden from directory | Change, or leave hidden on purpose |
| External members vanished after a settings edit | Allow external members turned off (Q2 2026 enforcement removes them permanently) | Turn it back on and re-add them |
| A form/alert sender "stops working" at busy times | 300 inbound per 5 minutes per group | Route automated mail to a user mailbox or split groups |
| abuse@ / postmaster@ refuse to be created | Reserved addresses | Create as aliases of an existing group in the Admin console |
| Attachment refused | 25 MB limit | Share a Drive link |
| Group deleted by mistake | No restore for groups | Recreate and re-share; Drive/Calendar access does not come back automatically |
